inline_comments.comment: The type annotation `atoms: Atoms` is incorrect — the function body explicitly handles the case where `atoms` is a `list`. This annotation will mislead type-checkers and users alike. Consider `atoms: Atoms | list[Atoms]` to accurately reflect the accepted types, or better yet, drop the `list` support entirely and require callers to unwrap their list before calling.

`plt.subplots()` is now called before the `isinstance(atoms, list)` guard (lines 105–107). If a caller passes an invalid list (length != 1), a matplotlib Figure is created and leaked before the `AssertionError` fires. The old code ran the list check first. Consider reordering: validate/unwrap `atoms` before potentially creating a new figure.

`plot_atoms_raw()` is referenced in the docstring as plain text. ASE uses Sphinx, so this should be a proper RST cross-reference — `:func:`plot_atoms_raw`` or `:func:`ase.visualize.plot.plot_atoms_raw`` — so it renders as a hyperlink in the generated docs.

`plot_atoms_raw` silently diverges from `plot_atoms` in that it does not handle a `list[Atoms]` input — passing a list will cause a confusing internal error deep in `PlottingVariables`. Either mirror the list-unwrapping logic here (so users can freely substitute one for the other), or add an explicit guard with a clear error message, and document the difference.

The third bullet in `plot_atoms_raw`'s docstring — 'set matplotlib axis properties directly by calling ax.set()' — does not correspond to any behaviour of `plot_atoms`; it is generic Matplotlib guidance. The "To reproduce the additional features of plot_atoms" framing implies each bullet maps to something `plot_atoms` does, which makes this bullet confusing. Remove or reframe it.

The changelog entry is filed under the "I/O" section, but these changes are purely about the visualization/plotting API. Check whether the project has a dedicated "Visualization" category in its changelog; if so, this entry should be moved there.

general_comments.comment: The `animate` function still uses `ax = plt.gca()` when no `ax` is provided (line 55 of the new file, unchanged). The changelog entry explicitly identifies `plt.gca()` as a hazard — 'possibly overwriting an unrelated plot' — as the motivation for changing `plot_atoms`. `animate` has the same footgun and was not addressed. Consider applying the same fix (`ax, fig = plt.subplots()` or similar) for consistency and to honour the stated rationale.

Because `plot_atoms` now unconditionally calls `ax.set_axis_off()`, the `ax.axis('off')` call inside `animate` (line 61, unchanged) is now redundant: every call to `plot_atoms(atoms, ax=ax, ...)` within the animation loop will set the axis off anyway. The redundancy is harmless, but it leaves stale code that may confuse future readers. If `animate` is updated to address the `plt.gca()` issue noted above, this line should also be removed.

The PR title refers to a function named `plot_only_atoms`, but the actual function added is `plot_atoms_raw`. If the name was changed during development, the PR title was not updated. This makes it harder to find this PR when searching by function name.

All checklist items in the PR description are unchecked (`[ ]`), including documentation, unit tests, and changelog. The changelog entry exists, but there are no new tests for `plot_atoms_raw` in `ase/test/test_matplotlib_plot.py`. A test covering at least the basic call path for `plot_atoms_raw` should be added.
